ruleset.name: skg-if-api
ruleset.description: Based on PMD's bundled category rulesets, tuned for this codebase to complement checkstyle (which only checks style/formatting - naming, whitespace, imports, javadoc presence). PMD catches what checkstyle structurally can't: semantic smells, duplication, and error-prone patterns. codestyle.xml and documentation.xml are intentionally not included - those overlap with what checkstyle already enforces. Rules disabled below produced large volumes of low-value violations on the existing codebase - see rationale comments, mirroring the approach in checkstyle.xml.

rule.name: SelfAssignment
rule.message: A variable/field should not be assigned to itself
rule.description: Equivalent to SonarQube/SonarLint rule S1656 ("Variables should not be self-assigned"), which has no build-time equivalent otherwise, since this repo runs no Sonar server - same rationale as NoNestedTernaryOperators/SeveralBreakOrContinuePerLoop below. Matches `x = x` where both sides are the exact same unqualified variable name - a copy-paste typo, not the legitimate `this.x = x` constructor/setter idiom (different name on each side, already excluded from HiddenField in checkstyle.xml) which this rule does not touch. Deliberately scoped to the unqualified-name case only (not `this.x = this.x` / `a.b = a.b` field-access self-assignment) to keep the XPath simple and avoid guessing at FieldAccess's exact qualifier-node shape.

rule.name: ExceptionCreatedNotThrown
rule.message: Exception/Error object created but never thrown
rule.description: Equivalent to SonarQube/SonarLint rule S3984 ("Exception should not be created without being thrown"), which has no build-time equivalent otherwise, since this repo runs no Sonar server. Matches a bare `new SomeException(...);` statement (constructed and immediately discarded) rather than `throw new SomeException(...);` - almost always a forgotten `throw` in a validation/error path.

rule.name: PreferSequencedCollectionAccessors
rule.description: Equivalent to SonarQube/SonarLint rule S6902 ("Prefer sequence collection getFirst() and getLast() over alternative approaches"), which has no build-time equivalent otherwise, since this repo runs no Sonar server. Since Java 21 (JEP 431), java.util.List is a SequencedCollection, so `list.get(0)` and `list.get(list.size() - 1)` should be `list.getFirst()`/`list.getLast()` - clearer intent and O(1) regardless of the underlying List implementation. Deliberately does not attempt full type resolution (PMD's symbol table is unreliable on generated-source-heavy compile classpaths per this ruleset's UnusedPrivateMethod exclusion above) - instead matches the syntactic `get(0)` / `get(same-receiver.size() - 1)` shape directly. This means it can, in principle, also fire on a non-List custom type with a `get(int)` method (e.g. a hand-rolled `Row`/`Tuple` class) - no such type exists in this codebase today, but if one is introduced, exclude that call site rather than removing the rule.

property.name: xpath

rule.name: IgnoredMethodResult
rule.message: Return value of a side-effect-free method call is ignored
rule.description: Equivalent to SonarQube/SonarLint rule S2201 ("Return values from functions without side effects should not be ignored"), which has no build-time equivalent otherwise, since this repo runs no Sonar server. Matches a bare top-level call to a small allowlist of well-known immutable-value-returning String methods (trim/strip/toUpperCase/toLowerCase/substring/ replace*/concat/intern) used as a standalone statement, where the only possible effect - the returned value - is thrown away. Deliberately narrow (name-based, not type-resolved, per the PreferSequencedCollectionAccessors rationale above) to avoid flagging genuinely void/side-effecting methods that happen to share a name - Stream/Optional's map/filter/ sorted/distinct were tried here too but dropped after a real `mvn pmd:check` run flagged CrossrefFilters#parse's `result.filter(...)`, a `ParsedFilter.Builder` setter with the same name as `Stream.filter` but genuinely side-effecting - too collision-prone to keep without real type resolution.

rule.name: NonShortCircuitBooleanOperator
rule.message: Use short-circuit &&/|| instead of non-short-circuit &/| in a boolean context
rule.description: Equivalent to SonarQube/SonarLint rule S2178 ("Short-circuit logic should be used in boolean contexts"), which has no build-time equivalent otherwise, since this repo runs no Sonar server. Deliberately does not attempt full type resolution (see the PreferSequencedCollectionAccessors rationale above) - instead matches `&`/`|` where at least one operand is syntactically boolean-shaped (a boolean literal, a `!` negation, an `instanceof` test, or a relational/equality/another boolean `&`/`|`/`&&`/`||` expression), so it doesn't fire on ordinary int bitmasking (e.g. `flags & MASK`).

property.name: xpath
property.value: //InfixExpression[@Operator = '&' or @Operator = '|'][ *[1][self::BooleanLiteral or self::UnaryExpression[@Operator='!'] or self::InstanceOfExpression or self::InfixExpression[@Operator = ('==','!=','<','>','<=','>=','&','|','&&','||')]] or *[2][self::BooleanLiteral or self::UnaryExpression[@Operator='!'] or self::InstanceOfExpression or self::InfixExpression[@Operator = ('==','!=','<','>','<=','>=','&','|','&&','||')]] ]

rule.name: MethodReturnsConstant
rule.message: Method always returns the same constant value
rule.description: Equivalent to SonarQube/SonarLint rule S3400 ("Methods should not always return the same value"), which has no build-time equivalent otherwise, since this repo runs no Sonar server. Matches a method whose entire body is exactly one `return <literal>;` statement - a method that can never do anything but return one hard-coded value. Deliberately scoped to a single-statement body only (not "every return in a multi-branch method is the same literal"), to avoid flagging methods with real, even if currently-identical-looking, branches.

property.name: xpath

rule.name: RedundantTrailingJump
rule.message: Redundant jump statement - already the natural control flow
rule.description: Equivalent to SonarQube/SonarLint rule S3626 ("Jump statements should not be redundant"), which has no build-time equivalent otherwise, since this repo runs no Sonar server. Matches a bare `return;` (no expression) that is the last statement in a void method's block, and a bare `continue;` that is the last statement in a loop body block - both redundant since control would fall through to the same place regardless. Deliberately narrow to these two shapes (not e.g. `break;` as the last statement of a `switch` case, which IS required there) to avoid false positives on the many contexts where a trailing jump is not redundant.

property.name: xpath

rule.name: NoNestedTernaryOperators
rule.message: Ternary operators should not be nested inside another ternary's condition or branches
rule.description: A ternary operator (`?:`) used directly as the condition, true-branch, or false-branch of another ternary is hard to scan at a glance. Equivalent to SonarQube/SonarLint rule S3358 ("Ternary operators should not be nested"), which IntelliJ's SonarLint flags locally (.idea/workspace.xml) but which has no build-time equivalent otherwise, since this repo runs no Sonar server. Prefer an extracted private helper method or an if/else block assigning to a local variable instead.

rule.name: SeveralBreakOrContinuePerLoop
rule.message: Loops should not contain more than a single break or continue statement
rule.description: A loop with more than one break/continue is harder to follow than one with a single, clear exit condition. Equivalent to SonarQube rule S135 ("Loops should not contain more than a single break or continue statement"), which has no build-time equivalent otherwise, since this repo runs no Sonar server - same rationale as the NoNestedTernaryOperators rule above. Counts only break/continue statements that actually affect THIS loop: a break belonging to a nested switch, or a break/continue belonging to a nested inner loop, is excluded. The exclusion is implemented as "no other loop-or-switch node sits between this loop and the break/continue" using the `>>` document-order operator, rather than an `ancestor::*[...][1]` "nearest ancestor" idiom - the latter silently mis-ordered results under PMD 7's XPath 3.1 (Saxon) engine in testing (breaks inside a nested switch were still attributed to the outer loop), since reverse-axis "closest ancestor first" ordering isn't guaranteed once the axis step is used as an operand rather than a bare path step. `>>` is unambiguous: for two ancestors of the same node, document order exactly matches nesting depth (the outer one always precedes the inner one), so "some blocking ancestor follows $loop" reliably means "nested inside $loop, closer to the break/continue than $loop is". Known limitation: a labelled break/continue that targets an outer loop from inside a nested loop is attributed to the nearest loop instead of its label target - not worth the extra XPath complexity since this codebase has no labelled loops.

property.name: xpath

rule.name: ReturnNullConsiderOptional
rule.message: Method returns null - consider returning Optional<T> instead
rule.description: Matches the "avoid returning null, prefer Optional" guideline (Effective Java Item 55), which has no build-time equivalent otherwise, since this repo runs no Sonar server. Flags a `return null;` statement, and a ternary `return cond ? x : null;` / `return cond ? null : x;`. No explicit void/primitive-return-type exclusion is needed: a void method's only return statements are bare `return;` with no expression, and a primitive return type can never legally hold `null` (a compile error), so both are already excluded by construction rather than by a predicate - validated against a real `mvn pmd:check` run (see below), unlike an earlier draft of this rule that guessed at a `ResultType`/`@Void` attribute shape that turned out not to exist in PMD 7's grammar and silently matched nothing. Deliberately does not attempt full type resolution (same rationale as PreferSequencedCollectionAccessors above) - matches the ReturnStatement/ConditionalExpression shape directly, requiring the null literal to be a direct child of the ConditionalExpression (its then/else branch) rather than merely a descendant, so `return x == null ? a : b;` (null only in the condition) does not match. This means it structurally cannot fire on a switch-expression `-> null` arm or a `yield null;` statement (those aren't ReturnStatement nodes) - intentional: this codebase's filter-clause-builder methods (FilterQuerySyntax#schemeOnlyFilter, DataCiteProductFilters/DataCiteGrantFilters#toClause, CrossrefFilters#toProductClause/ #toGrantClause) rely on exactly that shape and are marked @SuppressWarnings("PMD.ReturnNullConsiderOptional") rather than needing a separate carve-out. Known limitation: a block-bodied lambda's own `return null;` would be mis-attributed to the nearest enclosing method rather than being correctly scoped to the lambda - not worth the extra XPath complexity since this codebase has no block-bodied lambdas with a null return today; exclude that call site if one is introduced.
